display.purpose: The current day's name in the header — the single largest element on screen.

title.purpose: Progress screen title and the completion percentage.

body.purpose: Exercise names, set inputs, button copy.

label.purpose: Uppercase structural eyebrows: RPE, REST, DATA, SESSION LOG, etc.

shadows.name: day-glow
shadows.purpose: Marks the active training day's identity behind the header.

shadows.name: pb-glow
shadows.purpose: A card that just hit a personal best.

shadows.name: overlay-shadow
shadows.purpose: Floating toast/undo pills above the rest of the UI.

motion.name: pop-in
motion.purpose: New card/toast entrance: scale 0.92→1, fade in.

motion.name: gentle-pulse
motion.purpose: Rest timer at zero, prompting the next set.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default easing for done/PB/active state changes.

components.name: Primary Button (Finish Session)
components.description: Full-width success-tinted call to action that ends the session and saves it to history.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary">✓ finish session — save to history</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { width: 100%; padding: 13px 0; border-radius: 12px; font-family: 'SF Pro Display', -apple-system, 'Helvetica Neue', sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; border: 1px solid rgba(52,211,153,0.27); background: rgba(52,211,153,0.08); color: #34d399; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:active { opacity: 0.7; transform: scale(0.98); }

components.name: Ghost Footer Button
components.description: Low-emphasis utility action (reset / plates / progress) — the default for anything that isn't the primary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; color: #7d8595; background: transparent; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1); border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #f0f2f7; border-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.2); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #38bdf8; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Exercise Card
components.description: The core content unit: one exercise with its rest/RPE controls and set rows. Flat at rest; gains a colored top-bar and glow when complete or a PB lands.
components.css: .ds-card-exercise { background: #13161e; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.05); border-radius: 16px; padding: 14px; } .ds-card-exercise__bar { height: 2px; border-radius: 2px; margin-bottom: 12px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, #ff6b6b, transparent); opacity: 0.8; } .ds-card-exercise__title { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; color: #f0f2f7; } .ds-card-exercise--done { background: rgba(52,211,153,0.06); border-color: rgba(52,211,153,0.4); box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(52,211,153,0.2); }

components.name: Day Tab Chip
components.description: One of five day selectors in the header grid. Active state fills with that day's own tinted background, colored border, and glow.
components.css: .ds-chip-day { padding: 10px 2px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; text-align: center; border-radius: 10px; cursor: pointer; user-select: none; background: #13161e; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.05); color: #7d8595; transition: all .2s; } .ds-chip-day--active { background: rgba(255,107,107,0.08); border-color: rgba(255,107,107,0.375); color: #ff6b6b; box-shadow: 0 0 12px rgba(255,107,107,0.25); }

components.name: Set Complete Button
components.description: The 44×44px circular-ish tick that marks one set done; fills with a success gradient once ticked. Sized for one-handed, mid-set use.
components.css: .ds-set-complete { width: 44px; height: 44px; border-radius: 11px; cursor: pointer; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1); background: transparent; color: #7d8595; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; transition: all .2s; } .ds-set-complete--done { border-color: rgba(52,211,153,0.5); background: linear-gradient(135deg, #34d399, #6ee7b7); color: #000; }

narrative.overview:
Gym Tracker is a dark HUD you check under gym lighting, not a bright productivity app you check at a desk. Its base state is deliberately quiet: near-black tiered surfaces, low-contrast hairline borders, muted grey text. Nothing glows, shadows, or announces itself until something has actually happened — a set ticked, a personal best broken, a rest timer counting down. That restraint is what makes the payoffs (a gold PB flash, a green completion glow, a day's own neon accent lighting its tab) read as earned rather than decorative.

The five training days each carry their own accent color and gradient — coral Push, teal Pull, violet Upper, gold Arms, orange Legs — so the app's identity shifts subtly day to day while the surrounding chrome (surfaces, type, spacing, radii) stays constant. This is a solo tool built for one person's own programme, not a market product, so its "brand" is really a mood: technical, low-light, unsentimental.

Explicit anti-reference: this is not a corporate SaaS dashboard. No light backgrounds, no card-shadow-heavy admin-panel look, no blue-and-white enterprise palette. It is gym equipment, not office software.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, tiered dark surfaces (void → surface → raised → inset) instead of card shadows
Per-day neon accent colors that own their day's tab, header glow, and card top-bar — never borrowed across days
State-triggered glow (success green, PB gold) as the only source of elevation drama
Small, uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow labels (RPE, REST, DATA, SESSION LOG) as the recurring structural device
Single system font throughout; hierarchy comes from size/weight/tracking, not a second typeface

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Success green means done, gold means PB, sky blue means an active timer. Never recolor one of these three for an unrelated purpose, and never let a day's accent color bleed into another day.

rules.name: The Quiet-Until-It-Matters Rule
rules.body: Surfaces and controls are flat and low-contrast at rest. Glow, gradient fills, and saturated color are reserved for a state change (done, PB, active countdown) — they are the reward, not the wallpaper.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Any small structural label (not body copy) is uppercase, 10–11px, weight 700, with 0.08em+ tracking.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-Earned Rule
rules.body: A surface only glows in response to a real event (active day, just-completed, new PB, running timer). A glow on an idle surface is a bug, not a style choice.

dos: Do keep every day's accent color scoped to that day's own tab, header glow, and card top-bar — never borrow one day's color for another.
Do treat success green, PB gold, and timer blue as reserved semantic colors, not a general-purpose palette to pull from for new features.
Do use the uppercase/tracked label style (11px, 700, 0.1em) for any new structural/eyebrow text.
Do keep new surfaces flat at rest; add a glow only as a direct response to a state change.
Do keep the single system-font stack; do not introduce a second typeface for "emphasis."
donts: Don't add drop shadows to a resting card, tab, or panel — depth comes from the surface tier, not a shadow.
Don't push the interface toward a light/corporate-dashboard look (light backgrounds, card shadows, blue-and-white enterprise palette) — this is gym equipment, not office software.
Don't make controls smaller than the existing steppers/complete-buttons (~38–44px) — they're sized for one-handed, mid-set use, not desktop-precision pointing.
Don't add a second decorative font, icon set, or illustration style; the app's only "graphics" are emoji, SVG (chart + timer ring), and color itself.
